questions.prompt: A 4S2P pack of cells rated 3.7 V and 2.2 Ah. Energy in Wh. Precision 0.01.
A 2200 mAh LiPo is rated 25C continuous. Maximum continuous current in amps.
A 60 Wh pack, 80 % usable, drives loads that average 16 W straight from the battery. Runtime in hours.
Logic averages 10 W behind a converter of 80 % efficiency; motors average 5 W directly from the battery. Battery-side power in watts.
Worst-case current of three motors with 1.5 A stall current each plus 0.8 A of logic, in amps.
A 24 V supply must give 5 V at 1 A for a computer. Which regulator and why?
options: A linear regulator: it is simplest and gives the cleanest output at any voltage drop.
A buck converter: linear would burn 19 W as heat.
A boost converter, because the load needs more current than the source offers.
Neither: connect 5 V parts directly and let their own protection handle the rest.
questions.explanation: (24 - 5) x 1 = 19 W of heat in a linear regulator, so a buck converter is the right choice.

questions.prompt: A linear regulator converts 12 V to 3.3 V at 0.3 A. Heat in watts. Precision 0.01.
A buck converter delivers 10 W at 5 V from a 12 V battery at 85 % efficiency. Input current in amps. Precision 0.005.
Continuous current is 4.2 A. What is the minimum fuse rating in amps using the 125 % rule?
questions.explanation: 1.25 x 4.2 = 5.25 A; choose the next standard rating above it.

questions.prompt: A 30 A fuse is installed on a battery lead made of 22 AWG wire (about 7 A). What is wrong?
options: The fuse is too small and will blow every time the robot starts moving.
Nothing: a larger fuse always gives a larger safety margin.
The fuse exceeds the wire rating, so the wire can burn first.
The fuse must be placed after the motor driver, not before it.
questions.explanation: A fuse protects the wire, so its rating must be no higher than what the thinnest wire can carry.

questions.prompt: A 2S pack has open-circuit voltage 7.4 V and internal resistance 0.2 ohm. Terminal voltage at an 8 A surge, in volts.
Two boards, each with its own supply, are linked by a serial wire and exchange only garbage. Which check comes first?
options: Their grounds are connected, giving a shared reference.
That the baud rate is a multiple of the battery voltage.
That both boards use the same battery chemistry.
That the wire is thick enough for the fuse rating.
questions.explanation: Without a common ground the receiver has no reference for the signal level.

questions.prompt: A LiPo pack has swollen after a crash. What is the right action?
options: Charge it slowly to see whether it recovers, but watch it.
Stop using it, do not charge it, dispose of it safely.
Press the puffy cell flat so it fits the battery bay again.
Discharge it to zero with a motor, then charge it again.
questions.explanation: A swollen or damaged lithium pack is a fire risk: retire it, never charge it and never press or puncture it.

questions.prompt: In a normally closed E-stop chain, what happens when a wire in the chain comes loose?
options: Nothing changes until someone presses the button on the chain.
The robot keeps running but only logs a warning about the chain.
Circuit opens, contactor drops, motor power is cut.
The software is told and decides by itself whether it should stop.
questions.explanation: An open circuit is the same as a press: that is why normally closed contacts are fail-safe.

questions.prompt: Design the power system of a 2 kg two-motor robot with a 5 V computer: list the numbers you need, the parts in order from battery to loads and the checks you run.
rubric: Gives stall and rated motor current, computer power and the supply voltage, and sums peak current and average power.
Orders the path battery, fuse, E-stop contactor, buck for 5 V and motor driver, with a common star ground.
Computes runtime and checks sag and the cut-off voltage at stall, and names a measurement that would reject the design.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Write a test plan for a function that returns battery runtime from Wh, a usable fraction and a list of loads with efficiencies.
rubric: Includes a hand-computed baseline such as 40 Wh at 75 percent and 12 W giving 2.5 h.
Tests that runtime falls when power rises and that a converter efficiency below 1 raises the battery power.
Tests invalid inputs: zero or negative power, efficiency 0, duty above 1, usable fraction 0.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: A lightweight arm needs 40 A peaks for a few seconds and low weight. Which battery type fits best?
options: Sealed lead-acid, because it is cheap and tolerant of abuse.
NiMH AA cells, because they have the highest energy per kilogram.
A single alkaline cell, because it never needs charging.
LiPo with a high C-rate, fused, balance-charged.
questions.explanation: LiPo gives high power per weight; it needs a fuse, a balance charger and careful handling.
